description: Physical-modelling voice: three exciters — bowing, blowing and striking — feeding a bank of tuned resonant modes, with a stereo reverb after it

params.text: Sets the shape of the envelope applied to the bow and blow exciters, running from short decays through slower sustained shapes to fast attack-release shapes
Sets how much bowing noise reaches the resonator, raising the simulated bow pressure with it so the tone grows brighter and grittier
Sets how much granular blowing noise reaches the resonator
Sets how much percussive noise reaches the resonator; past about two o'clock some of it also bleeds straight to the output for a harder attack
Sets the fundamental in semitone steps, spanning five octaves
Detunes the fundamental by up to two semitones either way
Attenuverts the FM input, on an exponential scale that stays gentle near the centre
Sets the colour of the blowing noise, scanning a range of noise textures
Chooses what the striking exciter hits with, morphing through recorded mallets, modelled mallets, plectrums and bouncing particles
Sets the shape and stiffness of the resonating structure, from plates through strings to bars and tubes to bells and bowls
Sets how much the high modes are damped, low settings giving wood or nylon and high settings glass or steel
Sets the smoothness or granularity of the bowing noise
Sets the pitch and granulation rate of the blowing noise
Sets the brightness and speed of the percussive excitation
Sets how fast the resonator loses energy, which is how long a note rings on
Sets where on the string or surface the excitation is applied; in the middle the even harmonics cancel and the tone goes hollow
Sets the stereo width below noon and the amount and decay of the reverb above it
Attenuverts the bow timbre input
Attenuverts the air flow input
Attenuverts the blow timbre input
Attenuverts the mallet input
Attenuverts the strike timbre input
Attenuverts the damping input
Attenuverts the geometry input
Attenuverts the position input
Attenuverts the brightness input
Attenuverts the reverb space input
Runs the exciter and its envelope for as long as the button is held, which is what a high gate on the GATE input does

inputs.text: Sets the fundamental of the resonator, one volt per octave; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices the module runs, up to sixteen
Shifts the fundamental, scaled by the FM attenuverter
A voltage of 1V or more runs the exciter and its envelope
Attenuates the excitation, full strength at 0V and silent at 5V, the reverse of the manual, which has the voltage boosting the excitation
An external signal that takes the place of the blowing noise, passing through the envelope and the strength control on its way to the resonator
An external signal sent straight into the resonator with no processing before it
Modulates the bow timbre through its attenuverter
Modulates the colour of the blowing noise through its attenuverter
Modulates the blow timbre through its attenuverter
Modulates the mallet type through its attenuverter
Modulates the strike timbre through its attenuverter
Modulates the damping through its attenuverter
Modulates the resonator geometry through its attenuverter
Modulates the excitation position through its attenuverter
Modulates the brightness through its attenuverter
Modulates the reverb space through its attenuverter; a large voltage with the SPACE knob at maximum freezes the reverb tail

outputs.text: The resonator signal; as SPACE is raised this becomes the left half of a stereo pair
The exciter signal; as SPACE is raised this becomes the right half of a stereo pair

notes: the exciters make no sound until they are gated: hold the play button on the panel, or send 1V or more to GATE.
a new Elements has BOW and BLOW at zero and STRIKE half way up, so the first gate gives a struck sound until those two knobs are raised.
